speaker: Doctor
text: Can you describe exactly where you experience discomfort during sexual activity, and does this pain occur before or after penetration? How long have you been experiencing difficulties conceiving, and have you had any menstrual irregularities?

speaker: Patient
text: 30-year-old female. The patient and her husband have been trying to conceive for 15 months without success. They are sexually active at least twice a week. The husband occasionally has difficulties maintaining an erection. The patient reports discomfort and pelvic floor muscle tension during attempted vaginal penetration. Diagnosed with body dysmorphic disorder three years ago. No family history of serious illness. She is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. No medications.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those details; the combination of 15 months of infertility and pain with penetration suggests we should evaluate for endometriosis or pelvic inflammatory disease. Given your history of body dysmorphic disorder, we must also carefully rule out psychosomatic pelvic pain or vaginismus. REQUEST TEST: Pelvic_Ultrasound. Do you notice any worsening pain during your menstrual periods or with bowel movements?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Normal uterus and adnexa with no evidence of fibroids or ovarian cysts.

text: Past medical history: Body Dysmorphic Disorder diagnosed three years ago. Social history: Does not smoke or drink alcohol.

speaker: Patient
text: All other systems reviewed are within normal limits. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Multiple sclerosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Vaginismus. The patient's primary complaint is pain specifically during penetration accompanied by pelvic floor muscle tension, and the mention of Multiple Sclerosis is a red herring inconsistent with the absence of other neurological deficits and the specific nature of the sexual dysfunction. I request a pelvic examination to confirm muscle spasms and rule out endometriosis.
